deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is setting up the general theory of Banach sequence spaces built from a symmetric ('Schatten') or lattice ('Köthe') norm N on finitely supported sequences R^(N). These are the tools he needs for Schatten–von Neumann type operator classes, which are announced on the next page as L^N(E,F).

Setup from the previous page. For a sequence x, |x|_n denotes its truncation in absolute value. N(x) is defined as sup_n N(|x|_n), and ℓ^N = {x : N(x) < ∞}. Two facts were proved there:
- (6) ℓ^1 ⊂ ℓ^N ⊂ ℓ^∞, with both injections of norm ≤ 1.
- (7) The countable triangle inequality N(Σ x^k) ≤ Σ N(x^k). Its proof uses the lower semicontinuity (Fatou property) built into the sup-definition.

Completeness of ℓ^N. Grothendieck uses the absolutely-summable-series criterion. Suppose Σ N(x^k) < ∞.
1. Since N_∞ ≤ N, the series converges in ℓ^∞ to some x.
2. By (7), N(x) < ∞, so x ∈ ℓ^N.
3. Again by (7), N(x − Σ_{k≤n} x^k) = N(Σ_{k>n} x^k) ≤ Σ_{k>n} N(x^k), which tends to 0. So the series converges to x in ℓ^N.

A marginal note says this is superfluous: completeness follows anyway once ℓ^N is identified as a dual, namely of ℓ_{N°}.

The space ℓ_N. It is defined as the closure of R^(N) in ℓ^N, i.e. the completion of the finitely supported sequences under N. Monotonicity in N gives (8) ℓ^1 ⊂ ℓ_N ⊂ c_0, since ℓ_{N_1} = ℓ^1 and ℓ_{N_∞} = c_0.

Abandoned material. A proposition is begun: ℓ^N ⊂ c_0 iff a condition on N, presumably that N is not equivalent to N_∞. An attempted lemma (9) ℓ_N = ℓ^N ∩ c_0 is struck out with a large zigzag.

Duality. R^(N) is put in duality with itself via ⟨x,y⟩ = Σ x_i y_i. The polar norm is N°(y) = sup_{N(x)≤1} |⟨x,y⟩|. If N is a Schatten (symmetric) norm, so is N°. A struck passage begins the theorem that the dual of ℓ_N is ℓ^{N°}. The bottom margin fixes the notation N° =: N'.

The next page completes this programme:
- the Hölder inequality Σ|x_i x'_i| ≤ N(x) N'(x');
- (ℓ_N)' = ℓ^{N'} isometrically;
- ℓ_N is reflexive iff ℓ_N = ℓ^N and ℓ_{N'} = ℓ^{N'};
- the definition of operator classes L^N(E,F).

All of this is the standard theory of symmetric gauge functions and symmetric sequence spaces: von Neumann 1937, Schatten 1950, Köthe–Toeplitz; later Gohberg–Krein and Lindenstrauss–Tzafriri.
errors: Monotonicity is stated as 'si N' ≤ N'', alors ℓ_{N'} ⊂ ℓ_{N''}'. This is the wrong direction: a smaller norm gives a larger space, so N' ≤ N'' implies ℓ_{N''} ⊂ ℓ_{N'}. That is also the direction Grothendieck himself used on the previous page, and the one consistent with (8), since N_∞ ≤ N_1 and ℓ^1 ⊂ c_0. Probably a slip, or the image was misread.

The step 'x ∈ ℓ^N' in the completeness proof is asserted without comment. It relies on the countable triangle inequality (7) together with the Fatou-type definition of N on infinite sequences. This is fine but implicit.

The Proposition 'ℓ^N ⊂ c_0 iff ...' is left unfinished, and the attempted identity ℓ_N = ℓ^N ∩ c_0 is struck out. In general that identity is false; it fails, for example, for Lorentz/Marcinkiewicz-type symmetric spaces.

ideas.what: Completeness of ℓ^N via absolutely summable series and the countable triangle inequality (Fatou property)
ideas.modern_name: Riesz–Fischer property of Banach function/sequence lattices with the Fatou property

ideas.what: ℓ_N = closure of finitely supported sequences, with ℓ^1 ⊂ ℓ_N ⊂ c_0
ideas.modern_name: Order-continuous (separable) part of a symmetric sequence space

ideas.what: Polar/dual norm N° of a symmetric gauge function, again symmetric, with duality (ℓ_N)' = ℓ^{N°}
ideas.modern_name: Dual symmetric gauge function; Köthe dual of a symmetric sequence space
ideas.where_published: Possibly in background of Produits tensoriels topologiques (1955), unsure

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but standard development of symmetric (Schatten/von Neumann) sequence spaces and their duality. This was already in Schatten's 1950 book. It is preparatory material for operator classes L^N(E,F), and nothing here is new.
transcription_corrections: 'Proposition ... ℓ^N ⊂ c_0 si et si N est équivalent' most likely reads '... si et seulement si N n'est pas équivalente à N_∞'. The text is unfinished and partly struck.
'complété de C^(N)' should read 'complété de R^(N)'.
Left margin (top) reads approximately 'Inutile, il suffit de remarquer que ℓ^N est le dual de ...'; the end most likely refers to ℓ_{N°}.
Bottom-left margin reads approximately 'Dans la suite, nous noterons N° = N', ...'. This is consistent with the N' notation on the next page.
The struck block numbered (9), 'ℓ_N = ℓ^N ∩ c_0', is entirely crossed out with a zigzag. The polar-norm definition is the operative (9).
